name: Episodic Memory Defect Leukoencephalopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Episodic Memory Defect Leukoencephalopathy

criteria.description: Progressive episodic memory impairment confirmed by neuropsychological testing
MRI evidence of diffuse or patchy white matter abnormalities consistent with leukoencephalopathy
Exclusion of other causes of leukoencephalopathy such as demyelinating diseases, infections, or metabolic disorders
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with leukoencephalopathy (if available)
Subacute to chronic progression with episodic worsening of cognitive symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: progressive episodic memory impairment, MRI white matter lesions consistent with leukoencephalopathy, and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing and clinical course support diagnosis but are not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Diffuse white matter abnormalities on MRI
searchTerms: widespread white matter changes on MRI
mood changes like depression or anxiety

laboratory: CSF analysis typically unremarkable or mild protein elevation
imaging: MRI showing diffuse or patchy white matter hyperintensities on T2/FLAIR sequences
genetic: Possible pathogenic variants in genes related to leukodystrophies or leukoencephalopathies (e.g., CSF1R, NOTCH3) in some cases
other: Neuropsychological testing confirming episodic memory impairment and executive dysfunction

distinguishingFeatures: Genetic testing positive for known leukodystrophy mutations
MRI lesions with periventricular distribution and contrast enhancement
Presence of oligoclonal bands in CSF
MRI showing lacunar infarcts and microbleeds

redFlags: Rapidly progressive cognitive decline over weeks
Focal neurological deficits such as hemiparesis or aphasia
